matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, recompute the integer values of both sides of the equation and ensure they are equal; without this, you may accept an invalid equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a stick move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Skipping the arithmetic check and outputting a transformed equation that still does not balance.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a standard Roman numeral; otherwise the character is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you modify a numeral, verify that the new shape matches a known Roman numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V, leaving it with a single diagonal, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only relocate it preserving its orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When relocating a stick, keep its orientation unchanged.
matchstick.example: Using a vertical stick to replace a diagonal in an X, violating orientation constraints.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses one stick) and the destination character (which gains one stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Ensure the stick you move is taken from one character and placed onto another, affecting only those two characters.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral but not adding it anywhere else, effectively deleting a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; you cannot remove or add sticks to it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Never modify the ‘=’ sign; keep its two horizontal sticks intact.
matchstick.example: Altering the ‘=’ sign by removing one of its horizontal sticks, turning it into a ‘‑’ sign.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick between numerals, use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both characters valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a numeral’s value, consider the catalog of single‑stick transformations.
matchstick.example: Changing an I to a V by adding a diagonal without removing a stick from another character, violating the one‑stick move rule.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line starting with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the corrected equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the very end of your response, before any trailing whitespace.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required prefix ‘Correct version of the equation:’ in the final answer.

matchstick.title: Plus-to-minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains a ‘+’, you may move its vertical stick to another character, turning ‘+’ into ‘‑’ and adjusting the other character accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a vertical stick can be profitably relocated to fix the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from a ‘+’ sign but forgetting to change the operator, leaving an invalid ‘+’ with only a horizontal line.

matchstick.title: Advanced numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: When moving diagonal sticks, consider swapping them between X and V (or similar) so that both characters remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If a diagonal needs to be moved and both an X and a V are present, swap a diagonal between them rather than removing it from one alone.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change a V to an X by moving a diagonal from nowhere, resulting in an invalid V.

matchstick.title: Diagonal swap for 5‑unit adjustments
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides of the equation is exactly 5 (or a multiple thereof) and both an X and a V appear, you can correct the equation by swapping a diagonal stick between an X and a V, which changes the V’s value by +5 (to X) and the X’s value by –5 (to V).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 5, 10, 15, … and an X and a V are present, try a diagonal swap between them.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to make it an X without a source X, leaving the source V invalid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and forgets to check the resulting arithmetic balance.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always calculate the integer values of both sides after any proposed change and confirm equality before finalizing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks without considering the set of allowed numeral glyphs.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each stick move, verify that each altered character matches a known Roman numeral shape.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operators like regular characters and may inadvertently change their shape beyond the allowed set.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict stick moves to keep operators within the allowed forms; e.g., a ‘+’ can become ‘‑’ only by removing its vertical stick.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets to specify where the stick is relocated, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that every stick taken from a source character is added to a destination character, affecting exactly two characters.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks in a way that leaves the operator malformed or creates an undefined symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When modifying operators, only allowed transformations (e.g., ‘+’ ↔ ‘‑’) are permitted; never produce an undefined operator.
